text:
sarah: Hey team, ACME flagged a ~30% token delta between their dashboard and the invoice for last week. Dashboard shows ~1.2M served tokens but invoice billed ~1.6M. They think KV/prefix caching + continuous batching might be the cause. Can someone triage?

omar: thanks for the ping. Can you paste the customer org id and a sample request id from their dashboard?

sarah: org=acme-corp, sample request id=req_20260301_42. Customer says requests are highly repetitive (same product descriptions) so cache hit rate should be high.

jia: quick hypothesis: we have internal prefetches and batch collations that count towards billing but get filtered out of the per-route dashboard metrics. ie dashboard reports "served tokens" per customer request, while billing includes additional internal model requests (prefetch/pin) that are not attributed in the UI. I'll look at traces.

mike: also worth checking continuous batching behavior. If the runtime pads sequences to the batch max or emits warmup calls, those can inflate metered tokens. Not always visible in the per-route tokenized tally.

metrics-bot: [automated note] route=req_20260301_42, model=rwd-3b-quant, batch_id=batch_9876, observed_kv_cache_hit_rate=72%, internal_prefetches=128, batch_padding_extra_tokens=4500 

omar: that metrics-bot line is interesting — internal_prefetches=128 is non-zero. Sarah, can you ask customer for a short repro script (2-3 calls) that exhibits the discrepancy? Also whether they used `continuous_batching=true` in their request config.

sarah: customer provided a minimal repro. Posting their curl (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-quant","input":"Generate product blurb for X","continuous_batching":true,"max_tokens":60}'
```

Customer repeats that 1k times in a loop. On the dashboard per-run tokens ~50, but invoice shows ~70 per run averaged.

jia: thanks. I pulled the trace for req_20260301_42. Sequence: client request -> router -> batcher collects 8 requests -> runtime does prefetch for shared prefix to populate KV cache on the GPU -> runtime issues an extra lightweight generation call for the prefix (counts tokens) which is tagged as internal. The dashboard filter excludes internal-tagged requests from "customer served tokens" view, but our billing pipeline aggregates any generation call attributed to the customer's request path (including internal-prefetches). That explains the delta.

mike: concretely: each prefetch issues ~8 tokens and we did ~5 prefetches per 1k requests due to cache misses across shards and batch boundaries. That adds up. Also batch padding: when batch has one long request and others short, we do padding at kernel level; those padded tokens are billed.

omar: can we reproduce locally? Jia, any quick repro steps?

jia: repro steps I used: run the customer's loop with continuous_batching on a small cluster, enable verbose runtime traces: set env REDWOOD_RUNTIME_TRACE=1 and run loadgen. Example:

```
# run loadgen
python loadgen.py --endpoint=https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --token=sk-TEST --parallel=50 --n=1000 --continuous_batching

# on runtime host
export REDWOOD_RUNTIME_TRACE=1
tail -f /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep prefetch
```

You should see log lines like: `prefetch: shard=3 tokens=7 reqs=8 internal=true batch_id=batch_9876`

metrics-bot: [note] billing-attribute:internal_prefetch=true is not yet propagated to billing-aggregator v1. Billing aggregations currently sum all model token counts grouped by customer id + model, ignoring internal_prefetch flag.

omar: ok that's the root cause. Short term: we can advise ACME to disable continuous_batching or set `continuous_batching=false` to avoid prefetch inflation. Long term: we need to fix billing pipeline to respect internal tags or to mark those token counts as not billable.

sarah: customer asked for an immediate credit if we confirm. Can support issue a temporary credit and tell them the mitigation steps?

omar: yes, support can issue a credit. I will open a billing-ticket referencing internal_prefetch and attach traces. Suggest credit = billed_delta ~ 400k tokens = $X.

jia: engineering action items: (1) short-term: add an admin flag in billing-aggregator to subtract internal_prefetch tokens for specific customers (QA). (2) medium-term: change runtime to tag internal-prefetch calls with header `X-BILLING-EXEMPT: true` and wire through to billing-aggregator. (3) update dashboard to expose "internal model calls" metric so customers can correlate.

mike: FYI: also confirm that quantized model variants still report token counts the same way — we saw rare discrepancies there if kernels request partial KV repopulation. I'll add a test.

billing-bot: [ticket created] BILL-4321: Investigate metering deltas for internal prefetches. Assigned to omar + jia. Priority: P1.

omar: I'll handle the customer credit. Sarah, can you send the customer a short note: 1) apology, 2) disable continuous_batching to avoid further inflation, 3) we will issue a credit and keep them updated. Also ask whether they can run with `continuous_batching=false` for 24h to confirm metrics align.

sarah: sending message now. Thanks all. Leaving this thread open until Billing confirms fix.

mike: follow-up note for postmortem: measure the ratio of internal_prefetch_tokens to customer_served_tokens over last 90 days and add an alert if >5% for any single org.

jia: created a small unit test to ensure billing-aggregator honors `X-BILLING-EXEMPT`. PR coming.

omar: closing loop: BILL-4321 will track the long-term fix, temporary credit approved by finance. I'll post the credit id here once applied.

sarah: ack — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
